Sizing
  • 1 unit = 1.00u (1.2% of the roll, reset monthly up or down).
  • Normal play: 1u. LEAN (unproven model): 0u. Great play: up to 3u, only for a PLAY, sized by ¼-Kelly.
  • Never more than 4u on one game, the same leg in more than 2 entries, or 15% of the roll open at once.

Discipline

4 bet(s) above the 3-unit cap, 2 stake increase(s) straight after a loss. The system's real failure mode is not a losing run, it is what gets bet after one.

Calibration

When a bet was logged at X%, did it win X%? The gap is only real if this holds.

House rules

  • One unit per bet. Not two because you love it.
  • A bet needs a positive gap, not a big favourite. High probability is not an edge.
  • If nothing clears the bar, bet nothing. A no-bet day is a normal day.
  • Three losses in a row does not change tomorrow's unit.
  • The unit moves once a month, on the bankroll, never on a feeling.
  • Write the reason and the biggest risk before the result is known.
  • No parlays as strategy. Correlated legs are one bet, not several.
  • Don't chase a price that has already moved.

  • Settle a prop or pick'em: edge hq settle <bet id> win (spreads/totals grade themselves with edge grade).

Public pools % = SurvivorGrid consensus (Yahoo/ESPN pools), the closest live read on a public Splash field. Future cost = the drop in your best remaining season path from burning this team now.

How to read it: each row is a team’s remaining season, one cell per leg, numbers are its win probability there (horizon-widened — a December cell is a forecast of a line, not a line). Future value adds up how much better than a coin flip those spots are (only the part above 60% counts, because a 55% spot is not a survivor pick) — it is the same number the field model and the champion model use, and the teams at the top are the ones you want to still be holding in December. Cost to burn is what taking the team this week knocks off your best remaining path — the board’s “Future cost” column, shown here beside the schedule it comes from. The brightest cell in a row is the best spot the team has left. Holiday spots matter out of proportion: none left are a separate contest week with a short team list, and running out of eligible teams for one is the most common way a live entry actually dies. Free for = how many of your entries have not spent the team yet.

How past Circa champions played it

Leg-by-leg analysis of the 480 champion picks: average pick 75% to win; the #1 favourite only 31% of the time (top-2 48%, top-3 59%); their pick carried 27% of the field on average while the chalk carried 41%; only 5% of picks were under 60% to win. Chalk rate by season phase: 38% (legs 1–6), 40% (7–12), 17% (13+). Holiday legs: average 64% to win. Champions who owned several entries split them in 83% of legs where two or more were alive — and the extra entries went a rung or two down: average 72% to win (vs 80% for the primary), median #4 favourite, 38% of the time 10+ points below the primary, and a third of them on bottom-half future-value teams (e.g. 2025 Week 1: DEN on the main entry, ARI / JAX / PIT on the others).

Gold rows are teams the model suggests for one of your entries. Range is the 10th–90th percentile this projection has landed in out of sample — the grey block on the bar. Public pools is SurvivorGrid’s Yahoo/ESPN consensus, usually more lopsided than the model’s projection — blank this week because SurvivorGrid has not posted the new board yet; its homepage still shows the completed week, and last week’s chalk is not this week’s. Still have it is the share of alive entries that have not spent the team yet; a team most of the field has burned cannot be popular however good the spot is. Leverage is how much bigger your share of the pot gets if you take the team and it wins.

Tested by holding each season out of the fit and projecting it blind (50 legs with 500+ entries, 2021–2026): the model names the field’s most popular team 64% of the time and is off by 12% of pick share on it, and 21% of the field’s picks land on a team other than the one predicted for them. That is the honest accuracy of the range column — it is measured, not asserted, and it is why the range is quoted at all.

Where the number comes from

A conditional-logit choice model fitted to every Circa selections PDF since 2021 (the only pick-by-pick survivor data published anywhere), projected onto this pool’s surviving entries — 106 legs, each entry’s exact remaining teams as its menu, so a team two-thirds of the field has already spent is not projected as chalk. What it reads: win probability, where the team sits on the board, what the rest of that team’s schedule is worth, holiday legs it can still cover, kickoff slot, home/away, opponent quality, and two behavioural terms — the field gets chalkier right after a bloodbath, and shifts as the pool shrinks. Source: 3,619 alive after W5 (the pool's count); what they used in W5 is the pool's own pick %. Field learning: temperature ×1.01 (1.00 = the 2021–25 average field; higher = chalkier), chalk bias +0.14. Last leg killed 50.1% of the field, and a field that has just been cut leans chalkier, so the model pushes more weight onto the favourite this week.

What the field has already burned: KC 74%, BAL 59%, MIN 39%, HOU 33%, CIN 28%, SF 27%, JAX 20%, DET 8%, NE 4%, PIT 2%, DEN 2%, NYJ 1%.

The weeks where the field is projected to pile onto a team that is not actually good — it drew the crowd by drawing a bad opponent. Being somewhere else those weeks is cheap leverage: the one time in three or four the chalk loses, a big slice of the pot goes with it. Flagged: a team on 25%+ of the field that sits outside our top 10 and is playing a bottom-ten team, or any chalk under 60% to win.

How this is built. Field shares for later weeks come from rolling the pool's whole field forward through the same pick model that projects this week, so each week’s number already has the field’s earlier picks spent. The range is how far a projection that size has landed from reality this season; a projection months out is looser than that. “Our board” is the Power rankings tab. Pivots are teams that leg winning 60%+ with under 15% of the field, and never a team your entry has already used. The chalk is not expected to lose more often than its line says — the edge is that when it does, the field shrinks and you are not in the pile. The plan maximises the chance of getting through every leg, so it is often on the chalk; each card shows what a pivot costs in win probability.

Bear's $50K Survivor 2026 · looking past W6 (Week 6)

Look Ahead

A look ahead is a forecast of a forecast. Nothing on this tab is a pick, and the lines it prices do not exist yet — a future leg's number is this week's market rating widened for everything that can still happen between now and then (injuries, form, the line itself moving). Use it to see which weeks are thin, what a pick this week costs you later, and which teams to keep — not to commit. The week you are actually submitting is on This week's suggestions.
Every future leg is priced from the same market-implied ratings and Elo the rest of the site uses, widened by 0.32 points of spread per week of lookahead and tilted by each team's expected trajectory. The pool's field is rolled forward through the choice model (fitted on Circa's selections) from 3,619 alive after W5 (the pool's count); what they used in W5 is the pool's own pick %: 3,619 entries alive now, spending teams every week — 120 simulated seasons of 6,000 entries, each season sharing one outcome per game so entries on the same team live and die together. Survivor counts are projections with a few percent of simulation error around them and are shown to two figures for that reason. Your assumptions live in this browser only. Season Map

Every number re-prices on each rebuild (every 2 hours, every 5 minutes on game days): 6 of 272 games carry DraftKings' current line via ESPN (as of 2026-10-18 17:53Z); the rest use market-implied ratings re-solved from today's lines (recent weeks weighted most) blended with Elo, which moves after every result. Far-off legs are tilted by each team's expected trajectory (↑/↓ on the row) and widened for the movement history says to expect.

Every path on this map is a model suggestion, not a committed plan. The grid re-solves the best surviving route from the current numbers each time you lock a cell — it shows what the maths would do, not what has been entered on Splash. Only cells marked submitted / locked are real picks.
Under the win %, also show: Click a cell to lock that team for that leg; the rest of the season re-solves for the best surviving path. Click ✕ on a team to exclude it (injury, "never again"). Everything you set stays in this browser.
Stance: Numbered dots show which entries are on a cell. "Together" re-solves all alive entries as one portfolio under the stance (the same γ the card uses) so they do not all die on the same Sunday; your locks always win.

    Portfolio

    Portfolio play

    One pick per entry, chosen across all your pools together for the best chance of winning at least one of them. This week's games are played out jointly, so two entries on the same team win and lose together.

    Spread gives up at most 1% of the best chance to make losing every entry in one weekend as unlikely as possible. All-in is the strict maximum. At these odds your chance of winning at least one is almost exactly the sum of each entry's own chance, so the two differ by hundredths of a point; what spreading really buys is not losing everything on one upset.
